heading: IS 10262:2019 — Concrete Mix Proportioning, Guidelines (checked facts)
text:
IS 10262:2019 — Concrete Mix Proportioning, Guidelines (checked facts)
NOTE — Values summarised in Aptimizer's own words from IS 10262:2019, checked by Saurav Ambasta in Phase II testing against the PDF copy of the standard. Page numbers are PDF page numbers of that copy. This is not the text of the Code.

heading: Target strength for mix proportioning
text:
4.2 Target strength for mix proportioning
Under IS 10262:2019 Cl. 4.2, the target mean compressive strength is f'ck = fck + 1.65 S or f'ck = fck + X, whichever is higher, where S is the standard deviation and X a factor by grade (5.5 for M25). For M25 with S = 4.0 N/mm² this gives 25 + 1.65 × 4 = 31.6 N/mm², which is higher than 25 + 5.5. Checked on PDF pages 4 to 5.

heading: Assumed standard deviation
text:
Table 2 Assumed standard deviation
Under IS 10262:2019 Table 2, the assumed standard deviation is 4.0 N/mm² for M20 and M25 concrete. Checked on PDF pages 4 to 5.

heading: Approximate air content
text:
Table 3 Approximate air content
Under IS 10262:2019 Table 3, the entrapped air content for 20 mm nominal maximum size aggregate is 1.0 percent. Checked on PDF page 5.

heading: Maximum water content per cubic metre of concrete
text:
Table 4 Maximum water content per cubic metre of concrete
Under IS 10262:2019 Table 4, for a 50 mm slump the maximum water content is 186 kg/m³ for 20 mm nominal maximum size aggregate and 200 kg/m³ for 10 mm aggregate. Checked on PDF page 10.

heading: Adjustment of water content for slump
text:
5.3 Adjustment of water content for slump
Under IS 10262:2019 Cl. 5.3, the water content is increased by about 3 percent for every additional 25 mm of slump above 50 mm, or decreased by the same proportion for a lower slump; the adjustment can also be established by trial batches with the actual materials. Checked on PDF page 7.

heading: Volume of coarse aggregate per unit volume of total aggregate
text:
Table 5 Volume of coarse aggregate per unit volume of total aggregate
Under IS 10262:2019 Table 5, for 20 mm nominal maximum size aggregate with Zone II fine aggregate at a water-cement ratio of 0.50, the volume of coarse aggregate is 0.62 of the total aggregate volume. Checked on PDF page 8.

heading: IS 1172:1993 — Basic Requirements for Water Supply, Drainage and Sanitation (checked facts)
text:
IS 1172:1993 — Basic Requirements for Water Supply, Drainage and Sanitation (checked facts)
NOTE — Values summarised in Aptimizer's own words from IS 1172:1993, checked by Saurav Ambasta in Phase II testing against the PDF copy of the standard. Page numbers are printed page numbers. This is not the text of the Code.

heading: Water supply for residences
text:
4.1 Water supply for residences
Under IS 1172:1993 Cl. 4.1, the domestic water supply for communities with a population of 20,000 to 100,000 with full flushing systems is 100 to 150 litres per head per day; 150 to 200 litres per head per day applies only to communities above 100,000. The 150 to 200 litres per head per day may be reduced to 135 litres per head per day for houses for Lower Income Groups (LIG) and the Economically Weaker Section (EWS), depending on prevailing conditions. Checked on printed page 2 (PDF page 6).

heading: Water for flushing
text:
4.1.1 Water for flushing
Under IS 1172:1993 Cl. 4.1.1, out of the 150 to 200 litres per head per day, 45 litres per head per day may be taken for flushing of water-closets; the rest of the domestic supply covers drinking, cooking, bathing, washing and other household uses. Checked on printed page 2 (PDF page 6).

heading: IS 13920:1993 — Ductile Detailing of Reinforced Concrete Structures subjected to Seismic Forces (che
text:
IS 13920:1993 — Ductile Detailing of Reinforced Concrete Structures subjected to Seismic Forces (checked facts)
NOTE — Values summarised in Aptimizer's own words from IS 13920:1993, the edition held by the Phase II team, checked by Saurav Ambasta. The 2016 revision changed this clause; these are the 1993 values. Page numbers are printed page numbers. This is not the text of the Code.

heading: Where ductile detailing is required
text:
1.1.1 Where ductile detailing is required
Under IS 13920:1993 Cl. 1.1.1 (a) to (d), ductile detailing is required in seismic zones IV and V for all reinforced concrete structures; in zone III it is required only when the importance factor I is greater than 1.0, or the structure is an industrial structure, or the structure is more than 5 storeys high. Checked on printed page 1 (PDF page 6).

heading: IS 1893 (Part 1):2016 — Criteria for Earthquake Resistant Design of Structures, General Provisions a
text:
IS 1893 (Part 1):2016 — Criteria for Earthquake Resistant Design of Structures, General Provisions and Buildings (checked facts)
NOTE — Values summarised in Aptimizer's own words from IS 1893 (Part 1):2016 (Sixth Revision), checked by Saurav Ambasta in Phase II testing against the PDF copy of the standard. Page numbers are printed page numbers. This is not the text of the Code. The 2002 edition's values are in is1893_2002.md.

heading: Seismic zone factor Z
text:
Table 3 Seismic zone factor Z
Under IS 1893 (Part 1):2016 Table 3, the seismic zone factor Z is 0.10 for zone II, 0.16 for zone III, 0.24 for zone IV and 0.36 for zone V. Z is used in the design horizontal seismic coefficient of Cl. 6.4.2. Checked on printed page 10.

heading: Zone factors for some important towns
text:
Annex E Zone factors for some important towns
Under IS 1893 (Part 1):2016 Annex E, Bengaluru (Bangalore) is in seismic zone II (Z = 0.10), Chennai is in zone III (Z = 0.16) and Delhi is in zone IV (Z = 0.24). Checked on printed page 36.

heading: Design horizontal seismic coefficient
text:
6.4.2 Design horizontal seismic coefficient
Under IS 1893 (Part 1):2016 Cl. 6.4.2, the design horizontal seismic coefficient is Ah = (Z/2) × (I/R) × (Sa/g), where Z is the zone factor of Table 3, I the importance factor, R the response reduction factor and Sa/g the design acceleration coefficient. Checked on printed page 9.

heading: Approximate fundamental natural period
text:
7.6.2 Approximate fundamental natural period
Under IS 1893 (Part 1):2016 Cl. 7.6.2, the approximate fundamental translational natural period is (a) Ta = 0.075 h^0.75 seconds for a bare reinforced concrete moment-resisting frame building without masonry infills, and (c) Ta = 0.09 h / √d seconds for buildings with masonry infills, where h is the building height and d the base dimension along the direction of shaking, in metres. Checked on printed page 21.

heading: Design base shear
text:
7.6.1 Design base shear
Under IS 1893 (Part 1):2016 Cl. 7.6.1, the design base shear along any principal direction of a building is VB = Ah × W, where Ah is from Cl. 6.4.2 using the approximate period Ta of Cl. 7.6.2 and W is the seismic weight of the building. Checked on printed page 21.

heading: Importance factor I
text:
Table 8 Importance factor I
Under IS 1893 (Part 1):2016 Table 8, the importance factor is 1.5 for important service and community buildings such as hospitals, schools and emergency buildings; 1.2 for residential or commercial buildings with an occupancy of more than 200 persons; and 1.0 for all other buildings, which includes an ordinary residential building. Checked on printed page 19.

heading: Damping ratio
text:
7.2.4 Damping ratio
Under IS 1893 (Part 1):2016 Cl. 7.2.4, damping is taken as 5 percent of critical for estimating Ah in the design lateral force of a building, whatever the material of construction (steel, reinforced concrete, masonry or a combination). Checked on printed page 19.

heading: Response reduction factor R
text:
Table 9 Response reduction factor R
Under IS 1893 (Part 1):2016 Table 9, the response reduction factor R is 3.0 for reinforced concrete buildings with an ordinary moment resisting frame (OMRF) and 5.0 for reinforced concrete buildings with a special moment resisting frame (SMRF). Checked on printed page 20.

heading: Percentage of imposed load in seismic weight
text:
Table 10 Percentage of imposed load in seismic weight
Under IS 1893 (Part 1):2016 Table 10, the seismic weight includes 25 percent of the imposed floor load where the uniformly distributed imposed load is up to and including 3.0 kN/m², and 50 percent where it is above 3.0 kN/m². Checked on printed page 20.

heading: Imposed load on the roof
text:
7.3.2 Imposed load on the roof
Under IS 1893 (Part 1):2016 Cl. 7.3.2, the imposed load on the roof need not be considered when calculating design seismic forces, although the weights of equipment and other permanently fixed facilities on the roof should be included. Checked on printed page 20.

heading: Storey drift limitation
text:
7.11.1.1 Storey drift limitation
Under IS 1893 (Part 1):2016 Cl. 7.11.1.1, the storey drift in any storey shall not exceed 0.004 times the storey height under the design base shear, with the partial safety factor for all loads taken as 1.0. Checked on printed page 26.

heading: IS 1893 (Part 1):2002 — Criteria for Earthquake Resistant Design of Structures, General Provisions a
text:
IS 1893 (Part 1):2002 — Criteria for Earthquake Resistant Design of Structures, General Provisions and Buildings (checked facts)
NOTE — Values summarised in Aptimizer's own words from IS 1893 (Part 1):2002, the edition held by the Phase II team, checked by Saurav Ambasta. The 2016 revision renumbered these clauses and tables; these are the 2002 numbers. Page numbers are printed page numbers. This is not the text of the Code.

heading: Zone factor Z
text:
Table 2 Zone factor Z
Under IS 1893 (Part 1):2002 Table 2, the zone factor Z is 0.10 for seismic zone II, 0.16 for zone III, 0.24 for zone IV and 0.36 for zone V. Z is used in the design horizontal seismic coefficient of Cl. 6.4.2. Checked on printed page 16.

heading: Zone factors for some important towns
text:
Annex E Zone factors for some important towns
Under IS 1893 (Part 1):2002 Annex E, Bengaluru (Bangalore) is in seismic zone II, Chennai is in zone III and Delhi is in zone IV; the zone factor for each zone is given in Table 2. Checked on printed page 35.

heading: Design horizontal seismic coefficient
text:
6.4.2 Design horizontal seismic coefficient
Under IS 1893 (Part 1):2002 Cl. 6.4.2, the design horizontal seismic coefficient is Ah = (Z/2) × (I/R) × (Sa/g), where Z is the zone factor, I the importance factor, R the response reduction factor and Sa/g the average response acceleration coefficient. Checked on printed page 14.

heading: Fundamental natural period without brick infill
text:
7.6.1 Fundamental natural period without brick infill
Under IS 1893 (Part 1):2002 Cl. 7.6.1, the approximate fundamental natural period of a reinforced concrete moment-resisting frame building without brick infill panels is Ta = 0.075 h^0.75 seconds, where h is the height of the building in metres. Checked on printed page 24.

heading: Fundamental natural period of other buildings
text:
7.6.2 Fundamental natural period of other buildings
Under IS 1893 (Part 1):2002 Cl. 7.6.2, the approximate fundamental natural period of all other buildings, including moment-resisting frame buildings with brick infill panels, is Ta = 0.09 h / √d seconds, where h is the height and d the base dimension along the direction of the lateral force, both in metres. Checked on printed page 24.

heading: Importance factor I
text:
Table 6 Importance factor I
Under IS 1893 (Part 1):2002 Table 6, the importance factor is 1.0 for all other buildings, which includes ordinary residential buildings, and 1.5 for important service and community buildings such as hospitals, schools, monumental structures and emergency buildings. Checked on printed page 18.

heading: Response reduction factor R
text:
Table 7 Response reduction factor R
Under IS 1893 (Part 1):2002 Table 7, the response reduction factor R is 3.0 for an ordinary reinforced concrete moment-resisting frame (OMRF) and 5.0 for a special reinforced concrete moment-resisting frame (SMRF). Checked on printed page 23.

heading: Percentage of imposed load in seismic weight
text:
Table 8 Percentage of imposed load in seismic weight
Under IS 1893 (Part 1):2002 Table 8, the seismic weight includes 25 percent of the imposed floor load where the uniformly distributed imposed load is up to and including 3.0 kN/m², and 50 percent where it is above 3.0 kN/m². Checked on printed page 24.

heading: Imposed load on the roof
text:
7.3.2 Imposed load on the roof
Under IS 1893 (Part 1):2002 Cl. 7.3.2, the imposed load on the roof need not be considered when calculating the design seismic forces of the structure, so it is left out of the seismic weight. Checked on printed page 17.

heading: Design seismic base shear
text:
7.5.3 Design seismic base shear
Under IS 1893 (Part 1):2002 Cl. 7.5.3, the design seismic base shear along any principal direction is VB = Ah × W, where Ah is the design horizontal acceleration spectrum value (Cl. 6.4.2) and W the seismic weight of the building. Checked on printed page 24.

heading: Damping
text:
7.8.2.1 Damping
Under IS 1893 (Part 1):2002 Cl. 7.8.2.1, the damping for dynamic analysis of buildings may be taken as 5 percent of critical for reinforced concrete buildings and 2 percent for steel buildings. Checked on printed page 25.

heading: Storey drift limitation
text:
7.11.1 Storey drift limitation
Under IS 1893 (Part 1):2002 Cl. 7.11.1, the storey drift in any storey due to the minimum specified design lateral force, with a partial load factor of 1.0, shall not exceed 0.004 times the storey height. Checked on printed page 27.

heading: IS 1904:1986 — Design and Construction of Foundations in Soils, General Requirements (checked facts)
text:
IS 1904:1986 — Design and Construction of Foundations in Soils, General Requirements (checked facts)
NOTE — Values summarised in Aptimizer's own words from IS 1904:1986, checked by Saurav Ambasta in Phase II testing against the PDF copy of the standard. Page numbers are printed page numbers. This is not the text of the Code.

heading: Minimum depth of foundation
text:
7.2 Minimum depth of foundation
Under IS 1904:1986 Cl. 7.2, all foundations shall extend to a depth of at least 0.50 m below natural ground level. This is a minimum for every foundation; the actual depth also depends on the bearing stratum, scour, frost and movement of the soil. Checked on printed page 10 (PDF page 14).

heading: IS 456:2000 — Plain and Reinforced Concrete, Code of Practice (checked facts)
text:
IS 456:2000 — Plain and Reinforced Concrete, Code of Practice (checked facts)
NOTE — Values summarised in Aptimizer's own words from IS 456:2000 (with Amendment No. 1), checked by Saurav Ambasta in Phase II testing against the PDF copy of the standard. Page numbers are PDF page numbers of that copy. This is not the text of the Code. Only values that were checked are listed.

heading: Minimum grade, cement content and water-cement ratio for reinforced concrete
text:
Table 5 Minimum grade, cement content and water-cement ratio for reinforced concrete
For reinforced concrete under IS 456:2000 Table 5: mild exposure needs a minimum grade of M20; moderate exposure needs M25, a minimum cement content of 300 kg/m³ and a maximum free water-cement ratio of 0.50; severe exposure needs M30, a minimum cement content of 320 kg/m³ and a maximum water-cement ratio of 0.45; extreme exposure needs M40, 360 kg/m³ and 0.40. Checked on PDF page 33.

heading: Nominal cover to meet durability requirements
text:
Table 16 Nominal cover to meet durability requirements
Under IS 456:2000 Table 16 (read with Cl. 26.4.2), the nominal concrete cover to all reinforcement is 20 mm for mild exposure, 30 mm for moderate exposure and 45 mm for severe exposure. Checked on PDF page 60.

heading: Nominal cover for longitudinal reinforcing bars in a column
text:
26.4.2.1 Nominal cover for longitudinal reinforcing bars in a column
Under IS 456:2000 Cl. 26.4.2.1, the nominal cover to the longitudinal bars of a column shall be not less than 40 mm and not less than the diameter of the bar. Checked on PDF page 59.

heading: Nominal cover for footings
text:
26.4.2.2 Nominal cover for footings
Under IS 456:2000 Cl. 26.4.2.2, the minimum nominal cover to the reinforcement of footings is 50 mm. This is higher than the cover for columns (40 mm) because footings are cast against soil and are more exposed to moisture. Checked on PDF page 59.

heading: Partial safety factors for material strength
text:
36.4.2 Partial safety factors for material strength
Under IS 456:2000 Cl. 36.4.2, the partial safety factor for material strength at the limit state of collapse is 1.5 for concrete and 1.15 for steel. Checked on PDF page 81.

heading: Values of partial safety factor for loads
text:
Table 18 Values of partial safety factor for loads
Under IS 456:2000 Table 18, at the limit state of collapse the load factor is 1.5 for dead load plus imposed load (DL + LL), and 1.2 for dead load plus imposed load plus earthquake or wind load (DL + LL + EL). Checked on PDF pages 81 to 82.

heading: Short and slender compression members
text:
25.1.2 Short and slender compression members
Under IS 456:2000 Cl. 25.1.2, a column is treated as a short column when the ratio of its effective length to its least lateral dimension is less than 12; otherwise it is slender. Checked on PDF pages 53 to 54.

heading: Minimum eccentricity
text:
25.4 Minimum eccentricity
Under IS 456:2000 Cl. 25.4, every column shall be designed for a minimum eccentricity of l/500 + D/30 (unsupported length over 500 plus lateral dimension over 30), subject to a minimum of 20 mm. Checked on PDF page 55.

heading: Longitudinal reinforcement in columns
text:
26.5.3.1 Longitudinal reinforcement in columns
Under IS 456:2000 Cl. 26.5.3.1, the longitudinal steel in a column shall be not less than 0.8 percent and not more than 6 percent of the gross cross-sectional area (4 percent is recommended as a practical maximum). A rectangular column needs at least 4 longitudinal bars and a circular column at least 6, and the bars shall be not less than 12 mm in diameter. Checked on PDF page 61.

heading: Transverse reinforcement in columns
text:
26.5.3.2 Transverse reinforcement in columns
Under IS 456:2000 Cl. 26.5.3.2(c), the pitch of lateral ties shall not exceed the least of: the least lateral dimension of the column, 16 times the smallest longitudinal bar diameter, and 300 mm. The diameter of a lateral tie shall be not less than one-fourth of the diameter of the largest longitudinal bar and not less than 6 mm; the 6 mm figure is from Amendment No. 1 (PDF page 12), which replaced the 16 mm printed in the original clause. Checked on PDF page 62.

heading: Basic values of span to effective depth
text:
23.2.1 Basic values of span to effective depth
Under IS 456:2000 Cl. 23.2.1, for spans up to 10 m the basic span to effective depth ratios are 7 for cantilevers, 20 for simply supported members and 26 for continuous members. Checked on PDF page 50.

heading: Deflection limits
text:
23.2 Deflection limits
Under IS 456:2000 Cl. 23.2(a), the final deflection of a beam or slab, including the effects of temperature, creep and shrinkage, shall not exceed span/250. Checked on PDF page 50.

heading: Tension reinforcement in beams
text:
26.5.1.1 Tension reinforcement in beams
Under IS 456:2000 Cl. 26.5.1.1, the minimum tension reinforcement in a beam is given by As/(b·d) = 0.85/fy, and the maximum tension reinforcement shall not exceed 0.04 bD. Checked on PDF page 60.

heading: Minimum reinforcement in slabs
text:
26.5.2.1 Minimum reinforcement in slabs
Under IS 456:2000 Cl. 26.5.2.1, the reinforcement in either direction in a slab shall be not less than 0.12 percent of the gross cross-sectional area with high strength deformed (HYSD) bars, or 0.15 percent with mild steel bars. Checked on PDF page 61.

heading: Maximum diameter of bars in slabs
text:
26.5.2.2 Maximum diameter of bars in slabs
Under IS 456:2000 Cl. 26.5.2.2, the diameter of reinforcing bars in a slab shall not exceed one-eighth of the total thickness of the slab. Checked on PDF page 61.

heading: Maximum spacing of bars in slabs
text:
26.3.3 Maximum spacing of bars in slabs
Under IS 456:2000 Cl. 26.3.3(b), the main bars in a slab shall be spaced not more than 3 times the effective depth or 300 mm, whichever is smaller; distribution bars not more than 5 times the effective depth or 450 mm, whichever is smaller. Checked on PDF page 59.

heading: Short axially loaded members in compression
text:
39.3 Short axially loaded members in compression
Under IS 456:2000 Cl. 39.3, the design axial load of a short, axially loaded column is Pu = 0.4 fck Ac + 0.67 fy Asc, where fck is the characteristic concrete strength, Ac the area of concrete, fy the characteristic strength of the steel and Asc the area of longitudinal steel. Checked on PDF page 84.

heading: Flexural strength of concrete
text:
6.2.2 Flexural strength of concrete
Under IS 456:2000 Cl. 6.2.2, the flexural strength of concrete may be taken as fcr = 0.7 √fck N/mm², where fck is the characteristic cube compressive strength of the concrete in N/mm². It is used for cracking and deflection checks. Checked on PDF page 29.

heading: Modulus of elasticity of concrete
text:
6.2.3.1 Modulus of elasticity of concrete
Under IS 456:2000 Cl. 6.2.3.1, the short-term static modulus of elasticity of concrete may be taken as Ec = 5000 √fck N/mm², where fck is the characteristic cube compressive strength in N/mm². Actual measured values may differ from this estimate. Checked on PDF page 29.

heading: Curing
text:
13.5.1 Curing
Under IS 456:2000 Cl. 13.5.1, exposed concrete made with ordinary Portland cement shall be kept moist for at least 7 days; with mineral admixtures or blended cements, or in dry and hot weather, the period is at least 10 days. Checked on PDF page 40.

heading: Stripping time of formwork
text:
11.3.1 Stripping time of formwork
Under IS 456:2000 Cl. 11.3.1, with ordinary Portland cement, props to slabs spanning up to 4.5 m may be removed after 7 days, and props to beams spanning up to 6 m after 14 days. Checked on PDF page 38.

heading: Development length of bars
text:
26.2.1 Development length of bars
Under IS 456:2000 Cl. 26.2.1, the development length is Ld = φ σs / (4 τbd), where φ is the bar diameter, σs the stress in the bar at the design load and τbd the design bond stress. Checked on PDF page 55.

heading: IS 875 (Part 1):1987 — Dead Loads, Unit Weights of Building Materials (checked facts)
text:
IS 875 (Part 1):1987 — Dead Loads, Unit Weights of Building Materials (checked facts)
NOTE — Values summarised in Aptimizer's own words from IS 875 (Part 1):1987, checked by Saurav Ambasta in Phase II testing against the PDF copy of the standard. Page numbers are PDF page numbers of that copy. This is not the text of the Code.

heading: Unit weight of reinforced cement concrete
text:
Table 1 Unit weight of reinforced cement concrete
Under IS 875 (Part 1):1987 Table 1 (item 'Cement concrete, reinforced'), the unit weight of reinforced concrete depends on the steel content and lies between 22.75 and 26.50 kN/m³: about 22.75 to 24.20 kN/m³ with 1 percent steel, 23.25 to 24.80 kN/m³ with 2 percent steel and 24.80 to 26.50 kN/m³ with 5 percent steel. The commonly used 25 kN/m³ falls within this range but the table does not state it as a single value. Checked on PDF page 13.

heading: IS 875 (Part 2):1987 — Imposed Loads (checked facts)
text:
IS 875 (Part 2):1987 — Imposed Loads (checked facts)
NOTE — Values summarised in Aptimizer's own words from IS 875 (Part 2):1987, checked by Saurav Ambasta in Phase II testing against the PDF copy of the standard. Page numbers are PDF page numbers of that copy. This is not the text of the Code.

heading: Imposed floor loads for residential buildings
text:
Table 1 Imposed floor loads for residential buildings
Under IS 875 (Part 2):1987 Table 1, the uniformly distributed imposed floor load in dwellings is 2.0 kN/m² for all rooms and kitchens, and 3.0 kN/m² for staircases and corridors. Checked on PDF page 11.

heading: Imposed loads on roofs
text:
4.1 Imposed loads on roofs
Under IS 875 (Part 2):1987 Cl. 4.1 and Table 2, a flat roof with access provided carries an imposed load of 1.5 kN/m², and a flat roof without access (other than for maintenance) 0.75 kN/m². Checked on PDF page 18.

heading: IS 875 (Part 3):2015 — Wind Loads (checked facts)
text:
IS 875 (Part 3):2015 — Wind Loads (checked facts)
NOTE — Values summarised in Aptimizer's own words from IS 875 (Part 3):2015, checked by Saurav Ambasta in Phase II testing against the PDF copy of the standard. Page numbers are PDF page numbers of that copy. This is not the text of the Code.

heading: Basic wind speed at 10 m height for some important cities and towns
text:
Annex A Basic wind speed at 10 m height for some important cities and towns
Under IS 875 (Part 3):2015 Annex A, the basic wind speed Vb is 33 m/s for Bengaluru, 50 m/s for Chennai, 44 m/s for Mumbai and 47 m/s for Delhi. Checked on PDF page 54.

heading: Design wind speed
text:
6.3 Design wind speed
Under IS 875 (Part 3):2015 Cl. 6.3, the design wind speed is Vz = Vb × k1 × k2 × k3 × k4, where k1 is the risk coefficient, k2 the terrain roughness and height factor, k3 the topography factor and k4 the importance factor for the cyclonic region. Checked on PDF page 8.

heading: Terrain categories
text:
6.3.2.1 Terrain categories
IS 875 (Part 3):2015 Cl. 6.3.2.1 defines four terrain categories, from category 1 (exposed open terrain) to category 4 (terrain with numerous large, closely spaced tall obstructions). Checked on PDF page 8.

heading: Risk coefficient k1
text:
Table 1 Risk coefficient k1
Under IS 875 (Part 3):2015 Table 1, the risk coefficient k1 is 1.0 for all general buildings and structures with a design life of 50 years. Checked on PDF page 10.

heading: Importance factor for cyclonic region k4
text:
6.3.4 Importance factor for cyclonic region k4
Under IS 875 (Part 3):2015 Cl. 6.3.4, k4 is 1.0 for ordinary buildings, 1.30 for structures of post-cyclone importance and 1.15 for industrial structures. Checked on PDF page 12.

heading: Design wind pressure
text:
7.2 Design wind pressure
Under IS 875 (Part 3):2015 Cl. 7.2, the wind pressure at height z is pz = 0.6 Vz² N/m², with Vz the design wind speed at height z in m/s (from Cl. 6.3), giving the design wind pressure on the building at that height. Checked on PDF page 12.

heading: NBC 2016 Part 3 — Development Control Rules and General Building Requirements (checked facts)
text:
NBC 2016 Part 3 — Development Control Rules and General Building Requirements (checked facts)
NOTE — Values summarised in Aptimizer's own words from NBC 2016 Volume 1, checked page by page in Phase II testing. Page numbers are the printed page numbers of Part 3. This is not the text of the Code. NBC 2016 has since been replaced by SP 7:2026; these are the NBC 2016 values.

heading: Height of habitable rooms
text:
12.2.1 Height of habitable rooms
In NBC 2016, every room used for human habitation (living room, bedroom) shall have a height of not less than 2.75 m, measured from the surface of the floor to the lowest point of the ceiling, that is the bottom of the slab. For pitched roofs the average height shall be not less than 2.75 m. Checked on page 43 of Part 3.

heading: Size of habitable rooms
text:
12.2.2 Size of habitable rooms
In NBC 2016, where a dwelling has only one habitable room, its area shall be not less than 9.5 m² with a minimum width of 2.4 m. Where there are two habitable rooms, one shall be not less than 9.5 m² and the other not less than 7.5 m², with a minimum width of 2.1 m. Checked on page 44 of Part 3.

heading: Size of kitchens
text:
12.3.2 Size of kitchens
In NBC 2016, a kitchen in a residential building where a separate dining area is provided shall have an area of not less than 5.0 m² and a minimum width of 1.8 m. The kitchen height (12.3.1) is not less than 2.75 m, the same as a habitable room. Checked on page 44 of Part 3.

heading: Height of bathrooms and water-closets
text:
12.4.1 Height of bathrooms and water-closets
In NBC 2016, the height of a bathroom, toilet or water-closet (WC), measured from the surface of the floor to the lowest point of the ceiling (bottom of the slab), shall be not less than 2.1 m. This is lower than the 2.75 m required for habitable rooms. Checked on page 44 of Part 3.

heading: Size of bathrooms and water-closets
text:
12.4.2 Size of bathrooms and water-closets
In NBC 2016, a bathroom shall have an area of not less than 1.8 m² with a minimum width of 1.2 m, and a water-closet (WC, toilet) shall have a floor area of 1.1 m² with a minimum width of 0.9 m. A combined bath and water-closet has its own larger minimum. Checked on page 44 of Part 3.

heading: NBC 2016 Part 4 — Fire and Life Safety (checked facts)
text:
NBC 2016 Part 4 — Fire and Life Safety (checked facts)
NOTE — Values summarised in Aptimizer's own words from NBC 2016 Volume 1, checked page by page in Phase II testing. Page numbers are the printed page numbers of Part 4. This is not the text of the Code. NBC 2016 has since been replaced by SP 7:2026; these are the NBC 2016 values.

heading: High rise building
text:
2.38 High rise building
In NBC 2016, a high rise building is a building 15 m or above in height, irrespective of its occupancy. Height is the trigger for the high rise fire provisions of Part 4, such as two staircases, the firefighting shaft with fire lift (Annex E-2) and refuge areas above 24 m (Annex E-4). Checked on page 11 of Part 4.

heading: Doorways
text:
4.4.2.4.1 Doorways
No exit doorway shall be less than 1 000 mm wide, except in assembly buildings, where it shall be not less than 2 000 mm. Doorways shall be not less than 2 000 mm high. A revolving door is considered capable of exiting only 50 persons; a hinged door with the same exiting capacity must be provided in the same wall within 3 m of it; and doors shall not be located within 3 m of the foot or top of stairs or escalators. Checked on page 32.

heading: Corridors and passageways
text:
4.4.2.4.2 Corridors and passageways
Corridors and passageways shall be at least as wide as the aggregate width of the exit doorways leading from them in the direction of travel to the exit; no fixed minimum width is given here. In buildings with a central corridor that is part of exit access, room doors (except assembly rooms) shall open inwards. Checked on pages 32 and 33.

heading: Staircases, general
text:
4.4.2.4.3.1 Staircases, general
Every building referred to in 1.2 (high rise and the other listed buildings) shall have a minimum of two staircases. At least 50 percent of the staircases shall discharge directly or through an exit passageway. Minimum tread without nosing: 250 mm for residential buildings, 300 mm for assembly, hotels, educational, institutional, business and other buildings. Maximum riser: 190 mm for residential buildings (A-2), 150 mm for other buildings. Not more than 12 risers per flight. Checked on page 33.

heading: Internal staircases
text:
4.4.2.4.3.2 Internal staircases
Internal stairs shall be of non-combustible materials with a fire resistance rating of at least 120 min. A staircase shall not be arranged round a lift shaft. Minimum staircase widths: residential A-2, 1.00 m (0.75 m for two-storey row housing); residential A-1, A-3 and A-4 (apartments), 1.25 m. Checked on page 33.

heading: Travel distance
text:
Table 5 Travel distance
Maximum travel distance for residential buildings (Group A): 30.00 m for construction Types 1 and 2, 22.50 m for Types 3 and 4. For a fully sprinklered building the travel distance may be increased by 50 percent. Checked on page 32.

heading: 2 Firefighting shaft
text:
Annex E-2 Firefighting shaft
One firefighting shaft, with its staircase and fire lift lobby, shall be planned for each residential building or tower (Annex E applies to high rise buildings, 15 m and above). Checked on page 87.

heading: 4 Refuge area
text:
Annex E-4 Refuge area
Refuge area shall be provided in buildings more than 24 m high, at or immediately above 24 m and thereafter at every 15 m or so, sized at 0.3 m² per person for the occupants of two consecutive floors plus wheelchair space. High rise apartment buildings whose apartments have balconies need not provide refuge areas, but above 60 m such buildings shall provide refuge areas at 60 m and thereafter every 30 m. Checked on page 88.

code: Punmia, Soil Mechanics and Foundations, 17th edition
heading: Minimum depth of foundation by Rankine's formula
text:
24.2 Minimum depth of foundation by Rankine's formula
Rankine's formula gives the minimum depth of a foundation as Df = (q/γ) × ((1 − sin φ)/(1 + sin φ))², where q is the gross bearing pressure on the soil, γ the unit weight of the soil and φ its angle of shearing resistance. It is Punmia's Equation 24.8 in Section 24.2, page 677.
